findings.description: Detection at the instant the start limit expires conflicts with SYS-SUP-005 and CON-SUP-127, which treat a start delay equal to the limit as valid and allow detection up to 100 µs after expiry.
findings.requested_change: Align the detection condition and deadline with the equality rule and permitted measurement resolution.

findings.description: Detecting an overrun at the instant the execution limit expires conflicts with SYS-SUP-005 and CON-SUP-127, which permit execution exactly equal to the limit and allow detection up to 100 µs after expiry.
findings.requested_change: Align the overrun condition and detection deadline with the equality rule and permitted measurement resolution.

findings.description: The configuration CRC is stored in the same block over which the CRC is computed, but CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-129 do not identify whether the stored reference bytes are excluded or how they participate in the computation.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the exact byte range and treatment of the stored reference for the configuration integrity check.

findings.description: The requirement calls for one 1 KiB segment per cycle, while CON-SUP-107 permits an image of at most 1 MiB without requiring its size to be a multiple of 1 KiB. The final partial segment is unspecified.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the check handles an image whose length is not a multiple of 1 KiB, using an approved decision if needed.

findings.description: The requirement unconditionally drives the status high when start-up checks pass, including when the safe-state latch is set. CON-SUP-117 requires the safe state to remain latched until power-on reset, and CON-SUP-109 defines low as not operational.
findings.requested_change: Condition the operational indication on the absence of a latched safe state and other applicable faults.

findings.description: The reset obligation applies to any first or second detection, but CON-SUP-115 requires code 9 to latch the safe state, and CON-SUP-130 and CON-SUP-137 treat a code 8 start-up report as a latch-count event without initiating the normal fault reaction.
findings.requested_change: Specify the reset rule's applicable fault cases and its exceptions for configuration faults and code 8 start-up reports.

findings.description: The requirement applies the normal third-detection reaction to every fault code, while CON-SUP-130 says a code 8 start-up report does not by itself enter the safe state and start-up continues. CON-SUP-115 also latches code 9 on its first detection.
findings.requested_change: Resolve and state the applicable third-detection behavior for code 8 and the separate first-detection latch for code 9 using the product decisions.

findings.description: Safe-state entry, transmission of a report, suppression of a reset and retention of the latch are independently judgeable obligations; one can succeed while another fails.
findings.requested_change: Separate the independently verifiable reactions or reference separate requirements for them.

findings.description: The unconditional report within 10 ms conflicts with CON-SUP-121, which permits a watchdog reset to interrupt fault handling and requires only the subsequent code 8 report, with no report for the interrupted fault.
findings.requested_change: State the watchdog-reset exception and the required subsequent report consistently with CON-SUP-121.

findings.description: CON-SUP-139 gives fault reports priority over service answers, but the requirement does not define what happens when an answer is already being transmitted. Different interpretations could interrupt a line or wait for its completion.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable arbitration behavior for a fault report arising during an answer, based on an approved interface decision.

findings.description: The unconditional answer within 50 ms conflicts with CON-SUP-139 and SYS-SUP-050 and SYS-SUP-063: a request received during an answer is ignored, and intervening fault-report transmission extends the deadline.
findings.requested_change: Apply the request-acceptance condition and fault-report deadline extension to this response.

findings.description: The unconditional answer within 50 ms conflicts with CON-SUP-139 and SYS-SUP-050 and SYS-SUP-063: a request received during an answer is ignored, and intervening fault-report transmission extends the deadline.
findings.requested_change: Apply the request-acceptance condition and fault-report deadline extension to this response.

findings.description: The requirement reports SAFE from any fault detection until reset, while CON-SUP-130 and CON-SUP-137 say a code 8 report at start-up does not by itself enter the safe state and start-up continues.
findings.requested_change: Exclude the code 8 start-up report from the SAFE transition while preserving its contribution to the latch rule.

findings.description: The unconditional answer within 50 ms conflicts with CON-SUP-139 and SYS-SUP-050 and SYS-SUP-063: a request received during an answer is ignored, and intervening fault-report transmission extends the deadline.
findings.requested_change: Apply the request-acceptance condition and fault-report deadline extension to this response.

findings.description: The unconditional ERR response conflicts with CON-SUP-139 and SYS-SUP-050 when the invalid or overlong request is received while another answer is being transmitted.
findings.requested_change: Restrict the ERR obligation to requests accepted under the service-line arbitration rule.

findings.description: The count may be returned to zero only after 60 s of fault-free operation, but SYS-SUP-060 requires it to be cleared at any power-on reset, including before 60 s has elapsed.
findings.requested_change: Include the power-on reset exception in the count-clearing rule.

findings.description: The requirement mandates an answer to every service request, but CON-SUP-139 and SYS-SUP-050 require a request received while an answer is being transmitted to be ignored.
findings.requested_change: Apply the answer deadline only to requests accepted under the service-line arbitration rule.

findings.description: The requirement leaves the configuration bytes covered by the CRC and the treatment of the stored reference undecided. CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-129 do not resolve them, so a verifier cannot determine the expected CRC for a configuration block.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the covered byte range and treatment of the reference bytes, then state the decided coverage.

findings.description: The requirement calls for a CRC over one segment per cycle but does not specify how segments cover the image or how their results form the full-image CRC used by SYS-SUP-023. Rechecking one segment or independently calculating segment CRCs can satisfy the stated segment behavior without checking the full image.
findings.requested_change: Define the segment progression and the relationship between the segment processing and the completed full-image CRC.

findings.description: The requirement explicitly leaves fault-report priority undecided when a service answer is already being transmitted. CON-SUP-139 gives fault reports priority, and CON-SUP-112 requires a report within 10 ms; the required line behavior for this case is therefore incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Decide and specify the line behavior when a fault report arises during transmission of an answer, including its relationship to the report deadline.

findings.description: The statement combines independently testable reporting obligations for STARTUP, OPERATIONAL, SAFE and LATCHED with the separate obligation to count a code 8 report toward the latch rule. One state or the counting behavior could fail while the others pass.
findings.requested_change: Separate the independently testable state-reporting behaviors and reference the code 8 counting obligation in SYS-SUP-035.

findings.description: The phrase 'only after 60 s' prohibits an early count reset but permits the count never to be reset. CON-SUP-117 and CON-SUP-140 require the latch decision to distinguish detections separated by 60 s of fault-free operation, which cannot be assured if an old count persists indefinitely.
findings.requested_change: Specify when the count is cleared once the qualifying fault-free operating time has elapsed, consistent with CON-SUP-135 and CON-SUP-136.

findings.description: The requirement reports STARTUP from any reset until the start-up checks pass, even if a fault is detected during start-up or the latch is set. SYS-SUP-068 and SYS-SUP-069 require SAFE and LATCHED respectively in those cases; CON-SUP-130 gives LATCHED priority.
findings.requested_change: Specify the start-up reporting condition and state precedence consistently with CON-SUP-130 and the other state requirements.

findings.description: The requirement clears a code's count after 60 s of OPERATIONAL time since that code's most recent detection. CON-SUP-140 requires 60 s of fault-free operation, so a detection of a different code during that interval prevents it from being fault-free. CON-SUP-136 also permits bounded under-counting, whereas the requirement demands clearing exactly when 60 s have accumulated.
findings.requested_change: Define clearing using the fault-free interval and the permitted bounded under-count in CON-SUP-135, CON-SUP-136 and CON-SUP-140.

findings.description: The requirement mandates carrying a running CRC value from each segment to the next. CON-SUP-108 requires segmented processing and CON-SUP-129 defines the resulting CRC, but neither requires that intermediate computation method; the same whole-range result could be obtained by another method.
findings.requested_change: State the required whole-range CRC outcome without prescribing intermediate CRC state, or provide an approved source for the computation method.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-018 leaves the configuration bytes covered by the CRC and the treatment of the stored reference undecided. CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-129 do not resolve them, so a verifier cannot determine the expected CRC for a configuration block.
findings.requested_change: Specify the covered byte range, reference location and treatment of the reference bytes once the product decision is made.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-043 leaves fault-report priority undecided when a service answer is already being transmitted. CON-SUP-139 gives fault reports priority, and CON-SUP-112 requires a report within 10 ms; the line behavior for this case is incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Specify the observable line behavior when a fault report becomes due during an answer, consistent with the decided priority and timing.

findings.description: CON-SUP-117 requires the safe-state latch to hold the safe state until power-on reset. SYS-SUP-030 and SYS-SUP-065 set the latch, but the set does not require the outputs and status to remain low while it is set or prevent task release after checks pass. SYS-SUP-026 only holds outputs low until the checks pass.
findings.requested_change: Specify the controller's output and task-release behavior throughout the latched state, including after a software or watchdog reset, consistent with the required safe state.

findings.description: CON-SUP-132 specifies external pull-down resistors holding the three signals low and microcontroller pins remaining inputs until software configures them. SYS-SUP-026 requires low outputs and SYS-SUP-027 requires subsequent configuration, but the set does not capture the specified board provision or pin state during that interval.
findings.requested_change: Capture the external pull-down and pre-configuration pin-state obligations, with appropriate hardware allocation and traceability to CON-SUP-132.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 requires fault reports within 10 ms, and CON-SUP-141 identifies the classification instant for a code 8 report. SYS-SUP-039 applies its deadline when a fault is detected, but CON-SUP-137 says a code 8 report at start-up is not a fault detection; SYS-SUP-034 requires the report without a time limit.
findings.requested_change: Specify the applicable transmission deadline and timing origin for the code 8 start-up report, or record a blocking product decision if the source does not establish them.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-018 leaves the configuration bytes covered by the CRC and the treatment of the stored reference undecided. CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-129 do not resolve them, so a verifier cannot determine the expected CRC for a configuration block.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-003 and specify the covered byte range and treatment and location of the stored reference.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-043 leaves fault-report priority undecided when a service answer is already being transmitted. CON-SUP-139 gives fault reports priority, and CON-SUP-112 requires a report within 10 ms; the line behavior for this case is incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-004 and specify the line behavior when a fault report arises during transmission of an answer.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 requires fault reports within 10 ms, but SYS-SUP-034 requires a code 8 report without a time limit. CON-SUP-137 says that report is not a fault detection, and CON-SUP-141 identifies its timestamp but does not settle the transmission deadline.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-005 and specify the applicable code 8 report deadline and its starting instant.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 requires GET FAULTS to return the last eight fault reports. SYS-SUP-048 returns up to eight reports held in oldest-first order, but the set does not require the held reports to be the most recent eight.
findings.requested_change: Specify retention and replacement behavior so GET FAULTS returns the most recent eight reports, or all reports if fewer than eight are available.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-018 leaves the configuration bytes covered by the CRC and the treatment of the stored reference undecided. CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-129 do not resolve them, so a verifier cannot determine the expected CRC for a configuration block.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a product decision on the covered byte range and treatment of the reference, then specify them.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-043 leaves fault-report priority undecided when a service answer is already being transmitted. CON-SUP-139 gives fault reports priority, and CON-SUP-112 requires a report within 10 ms; the line behavior for this case is incomplete.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a product decision on line behavior when a fault report arises during an answer, and specify the resulting priority and timing.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 requires fault reports within 10 ms, but SYS-SUP-034 requires a code 8 report without a time limit. CON-SUP-137 says that report is not a fault detection, and CON-SUP-141 identifies its timestamp but does not settle the transmission deadline.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a product decision on the code 8 report deadline and its starting instant, then specify the applicable timing.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 specifies the FLT line format for fault reports, including code 8. SYS-SUP-034 requires a code 8 report, but SYS-SUP-039 requires the FLT format only when a fault is detected; CON-SUP-137 says the code 8 report is not a fault detection.
findings.requested_change: Specify that the code 8 report uses the required FLT line format and termination.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-018 leaves the configuration bytes covered by the CRC and the treatment of the stored reference undecided. CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-129 do not resolve them, so the expected CRC for a configuration block cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision on the covered byte range, reference location and treatment of the reference bytes, then specify them so the check can be verified.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-043 leaves fault-report priority undecided when a service answer is already being transmitted. CON-SUP-139 gives fault reports priority, while CON-SUP-112 requires a report within 10 ms; the line behavior in this case remains unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision on transmission behavior when a fault report arises during an answer, and specify the resulting line behavior and timing.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-034 requires a code 8 report without a transmission deadline. CON-SUP-112 specifies a 10 ms deadline from detection, but CON-SUP-137 says a code 8 report is not a fault detection; CON-SUP-141 specifies its timestamp without settling the deadline.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a decision on whether the code 8 report has a transmission deadline and its starting instant, then state the applicable requirement.

findings.description: The requirement mandates window-watchdog refresh while every supervised task is healthy, including when a non-task fault such as a code-integrity fault has been detected. SYS-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-121 prohibit watchdog servicing from fault detection until reset.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the refresh obligation so it does not apply after a fault has been detected.

findings.description: The requirement mandates independent-watchdog servicing while every supervised task is healthy, including when a non-task fault has been detected. SYS-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-121 prohibit watchdog servicing from fault detection until reset.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the servicing obligation so it does not apply after a fault has been detected.

findings.description: The requirement gives no deadline for sending the reset-cause message after classification. A verifier observing that no message has arrived cannot determine when the requirement has failed. OP-SYS-001 defers this missing limit even though it is needed to verify the obligation.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-001 as blocking and obtain an observable deadline for the start-up message.

findings.description: The default task set, release order, start limits and execution limits are independently judgeable: for example, the task set can be correct while an execution limit is wrong.
findings.requested_change: Separate the independently verifiable default configuration obligations or reference a controlled configuration table whose entries can be judged independently.

findings.description: The answer deadline, selection and ordering of reports, END termination, empty-history response and replacement of the oldest stored report can fail independently, but are combined in one obligation.
findings.requested_change: Separate the response timing, response content and history replacement obligations into independently verifiable requirements.

findings.description: The requirement does not say when the most recent eight reports are selected. CON-SUP-143 permits a new fault report to be transmitted between lines of a GET FAULTS answer, so the history can change while the answer is being sent.
findings.requested_change: Define the point at which the fault history for a GET FAULTS answer is selected, including how reports made during that answer are treated.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-081 requires an answer whenever GET FAULTS is received. CON-SUP-139 and SYS-SUP-050 require a request received while an answer is being transmitted to be ignored without an answer.
findings.requested_change: Restrict the GET FAULTS answer obligation to requests received while no answer is being transmitted.

findings.description: The requirement gives no deadline for sending the reset-cause message after classification. OP-SYS-001 defers the missing limit, but an observer cannot determine when the obligation has failed.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-001 as blocking.

findings.description: CON-SUP-133 limits the board output stage to 1 ms from pin change to output level. SYS-SUP-025 specifies the 49 ms software allocation, and SYS-SUP-024 specifies the overall 50 ms reaction, but the set does not state the intervening board output-stage limit.
findings.requested_change: Include the specified board output-stage limit and trace it to CON-SUP-133.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 specifies 100 µs measurement resolution for task timing. SYS-SUP-002, SYS-SUP-003 and SYS-SUP-056 specify detection deadlines, but the set does not require that measurement resolution.
findings.requested_change: Capture the specified timing measurement resolution and trace it to CON-SUP-103.

findings.description: The system requirement set does not capture or disposition the target microcontroller in CON-SUP-001 or the C11, no dynamic allocation and no recursion constraints in CON-SUP-004. These constraints are needed by downstream engineering.
findings.requested_change: Record and trace these constraints in the system baseline, or explicitly allocate their disposition to the appropriate downstream stage.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-029, SYS-SUP-030, SYS-SUP-064 and SYS-SUP-065 condition the response on there being no 60 s of fault-free operation since the first detection. SYS-SUP-059 clears a count only after 60 s since the most recent detection of any code. Detections at 0, 59 and 118 seconds can therefore leave the count at three while failing the third-detection condition, contrary to CON-SUP-140.
findings.requested_change: Align the reset and latch conditions with the per-code count and the fault-free interval specified by CON-SUP-135 and CON-SUP-140.

CON-SUP-130 says the report does not by itself enter the safe state, but also counts toward the latch rule.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the code 8 start-up behavior so that the ordinary report and the third-detection latch case have consistent obligations.

findings.description: The checked range is stated as from __app_start to __app_end, but neither the requirement nor CON-SUP-107 defines whether the byte at __app_end is included. Different interpretations produce different CRC values.

findings.description: The reset obligation has no exception for a watchdog reset interrupting fault handling. CON-SUP-121 permits that reset before the original report and safe-state entry complete and requires no original fault report; SYS-SUP-039 reflects that exception, leaving the deadline in SYS-SUP-029 without its stated starting event.
findings.requested_change: Limit the software-reset obligation to the case where fault handling completes before an intervening watchdog reset, consistent with CON-SUP-121.

findings.description: The requirement combines measurement of start delay and execution time at 100 µs resolution. One measurement can meet that resolution while the other fails, so the two obligations are independently judgeable.
findings.requested_change: Separate the start-delay and execution-time measurement obligations so each can be verified independently.

findings.description: The CRC range is stated as from __app_start to __app_end, but CON-SUP-107, CON-SUP-124 and CON-SUP-129 do not say whether the byte at __app_end is included. The two interpretations produce different CRC inputs, so the requirement cannot be verified consistently.
findings.requested_change: Once the product owner decides, specify whether the byte at __app_end is included in the checked range.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107, CON-SUP-124 and CON-SUP-129 do not establish whether the byte at __app_end is included in the CRC input. SYS-SUP-016 therefore admits different CRC inputs.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-004 and specify the program-code CRC range endpoints.

findings.description: CON-SUP-142 defines the configuration CRC range using __cfg_start and __cfg_end but does not establish whether the byte at __cfg_end is included. SYS-SUP-018 therefore admits different CRC inputs. OP-SYS-004 addresses the application range, not the configuration range.
findings.requested_change: Record a blocking open point for the configuration-range endpoint and specify the endpoint after the product decision.
